full_judgment:
12. We have heard the learned Advocates. It may be recalled that the people of undivided India, after a very long arduous and tortuous political movement, got their independence from the British yoke in 1947 by the Indian Independence Act, 1947 and the dominions of India and Pakistan emerged. India got its Constitution in 1949 and became a Republic in 1950. The political history of Pakistan was not that happy. It got its first Constitution in 1956, only to be ditched unceremoniously in 1958. Another Constitution was made in 1962 but again Field Martial (self appointed) Ayub Khan, in violation of the Constitution, handed over the office of President to General Yahya Khan in 1969. A general election was held in 1970, the first as well as the last in the erstwhile Pakistan but when the army President refused to convene the Constituent Assembly, rather, let loose a genocide in the then East Pakistan, independence of Bangladesh was proclaimed on the night following 25th March, 1971, and the People's Republic of Bangladesh was proclaimed through a historic war of liberation against the Pakistan Army and its murderous local vassals, and achieved its independence at a cost of three million martyrs on the 16th day of December, 1971. 

 73. This provision has an unhappy history. The framers of the Constitutions are aware about the unfortunate saga of floor crossings of the members in the Provincial Assembly in mid 1950s, bringing down the successive Governments one after the other. This sad experience must have loomed large in the minds of the framers of the Constitution. Dr Kamal Hossain admitted it.
